# C8 — Missing Reuse

*Level 1 card. 4 root causes. Open the level-2 card before accepting any of them.*

Energy waste from failing to store and reuse results of expensive computations, lookups, or data fetches, causing the same work to be repeated across calls, requests, or access sites. This includes not caching deterministic function results for repeated identical inputs (missing memoization), not pre-computing and storing derived artifacts like compiled regex or parsed configs (missing derived-value reuse), not caching chained attribute/scope lookups in local variables in hot code (missing local lookup caching), and repeatedly fetching the same data from external sources when local caching would eliminate the round-trip (redundant data fetching). Distinguished from Redundant Computation (C1) by spanning across calls or access sites rather than within a single scope.

## Root causes in this category

| ID | Name | The repair | Measurable? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **C8.S1** | Missing Memoization Cache | memoise the function | yes, scales with call count |
| **C8.S2** | Missing Derived-Value Reuse | build it once at module or class scope and reuse it | yes, scales with call count |
| **C8.S3** | Missing Local Lookup Caching | bind the resolved value to a local before the loop | yes, scales with input |
| **C8.S4** | Redundant Data Fetching | fetch once and reuse, with a TTL if freshness matters | yes, scales with call count |

Card paths: `reference/root-causes/C8.S1.md`, `reference/root-causes/C8.S2.md`, `reference/root-causes/C8.S3.md`, `reference/root-causes/C8.S4.md`

## Telling this category from its neighbours

These come up often enough to check before you commit:

- **C8.S1 vs C1.S4 Repeated Computation** — C1.S4 is repetition inside one scope, repaired with a local variable. C8.S1 is repetition across invocations, repaired with a cache that outlives the call.
- **C8.S1 vs C7.S2 Inefficient Problem Decomposition** — C7.S2 when the repetition is inside a single top-level call's recursion tree.  C8.S1 when it is across independent top-level calls.
- **C8.S2 vs C3.S3 Inefficient Per-Iteration Setup** — Both hoist; the difference is the destination.  C3.S3 hoists to just above a loop inside the same function.  C8.S2 hoists all the way to module or class scope so the artefact survives across calls.
- **C8.S3 vs C3.S2 Recomputing Loop-Invariant Values** — C8.S3 hoists a pure *lookup* with no computation.  C3.S2 hoists an actual *computation*.  `self.config.limit` is C8.S3; `len(xs) * scale` is C3.S2.
- **C8.S3 vs C10.S5 Inefficient Scope Lookup** — These are nearly the same repair.  Prefer C8.S3 when the target is an attribute chain; prefer C10.S5 when it is a module-level global or builtin whose cost is the LEGB walk itself.
- **C8.S4 vs C9.S3 Inefficient Retrieval Paths** — C8.S4 removes repeated I/O by *caching* a result that does not change.  C9.S3 removes it by *batching* many distinct requests into one.  Ask whether the repeated calls ask for the same thing (C8.S4) or for different things (C9.S3).
- **C8.S4 vs C9.S1 Fragmented I/O Calls** — C8.S4 removes *repeat* fetches of the same data.  C9.S1 keeps every distinct operation but *batches* them into fewer round-trips.

## If nothing here fits

Say so and move on. Reporting a weak match from an already-open category is the most common way this analysis goes wrong: the category is open because a static signal pointed at it, not because a smell is there.
